programme.title: Bachelor of Computer Science and Engineering
programme.teaching_language: English (English track). A second, Dutch-English bilingual track also exists; page text: 'Dutch-English track: Dutch and English / English track: English'. Students with a foreign diploma are admissible only to the English track unless they meet the Dutch requirements of the bilingual track (selection-procedure page).
programme.campus: TU Delft campus, Delft (single campus); programme page states 'Form: Full time - on campus'. Official programme name is 'Computer Science and Engineering' (closest equivalent of 'computer science'; Dutch name 'Technische Informatica').
programme.how_found: Web search 'TU Delft Computer Science and Engineering bachelor programme' (site:tudelft.nl) -> first result, the official programme page; facts under its 'Language', 'Numerus fixus', 'Start', 'Form' and 'Important dates' blocks.

english.quote: TOEFL iBT 90 (internet based), or IELTS 6.5 (Academic version, Overall Band Score), or University of Cambridge Certificate of Proficiency in English (CPE) or Certificate in Advanced English (CAE).
english.how_found: Programme page -> 'Admission requirements' -> 'More information about admission requirements for students from abroad.' -> BSc International admission-requirements page, section '2 Language Requirements' under the heading 'Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science and Engineering, Nanobiology and Applied Earth Sciences' -> 'Proficiency in English*'. Also surfaced by search 'TU Delft bachelor international students English language requirements IELTS TOEFL'.
english.notes: Requirements apply to all English-taught BSc programmes incl. Computer Science and Engineering. Preceding sentence on the page: 'You are required to pass one of the following language tests with the indicated minimum score requirement:'. No IELTS per-section minimum is published (only 'Overall Band Score'); Duolingo is not listed (only TOEFL iBT, IELTS Academic, Cambridge CPE/CAE). Certificates older than two years at the time of upload are not accepted. Exemptions: nationals of USA, UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, Canada; IB/EB/Surinam VWO/European pre-university diplomas with English as a final exam subject. A Kazakhstan NIS diploma does not fall under these exemptions, so a test is required.

value.description: No minimum GPA/grade threshold is published. Admission is by (a) diploma equivalence to the Dutch VWO with Mathematics as a passed final-exam subject, determined by the Admission Office after registration, and (b) a numerus-fixus Matching & Selection procedure (tests in Mathematics and Systematic Reasoning & Logical Thinking) whose ranking number is based on test results plus a lottery draw; 590 places for 2027-2028 (345 English track, 245 bilingual).

gpa.quote: The Computer Science & Engineering bachelor's programme at TU Delft has a Matching & Selection (Numerus Fixus) procedure. This means that only a limited number of spots are available, and all candidates are selected via the Matching & Selection procedure.
gpa.how_found: Programme page -> 'Information numerus fixus' / 'Selection procedure' link in the 'From application to enrollment' menu -> Matching & Selection CSE page.
gpa.notes: Same page: 'Your ranking number will be based on your test results and a lottery draw.' CSE admission-requirements page (https://www.tudelft.nl/en/onderwijs/opleidingen/bachelors/computer-science-and-engineering/bachelor-of-computer-science-and-engineering/from-application-to-enrollment/admission-requirements): 'You may be admitted with an international diploma if it is equivalent to a Dutch VWO diploma with the correct subjects. TU Delft will determine this after registration.' The BSc International page's country list does not include Kazakhstan; it says 'Is your diploma not in the list above? Get in touch with the Admission Office to find out about your options: contactcentre-esa@tudelft.nl'. Required subject for CSE: Mathematics (Dutch 'Maths B' level); Physics is not required for CSE.

deadline.quote: The application opens in October 2026 and closes on 15 January 2027.
deadline.how_found: Programme page -> 'Selection procedure' (From application to enrollment menu) -> Matching & Selection CSE page, first paragraph and 'Important dates' block ('Apply via Studielink: Until 15 January (23:59 CET)', 'Procedure 2027/2028').
deadline.notes: This is the 2027/28-cycle numerus fixus deadline (register in Studielink by 15 January 2027, 23:59 CET). International-diploma applicants must also submit a complete application file in the TU Delft system (Osiris) by 15 January. The programme overview page shows 'Numerus fixus : January 15th' and the application-procedure page states 'The deadline for numerus clausus programmes is 15 January, for other programmes the deadline is 1 April.' Ranking numbers are issued 15 April via Studielink.

tuition.quote: Institutional rate 2026/2027 2027/2028 Institutional rate BSc € 19.906 MSc € 25.633 BSc € 20.563 MSc € 26.479
tuition.how_found: Web search 'TU Delft tuition fees bachelor non-EU 2027-2028' (site:tudelft.nl) -> 'Tuition Fee & Finances' page -> 'Institutional rate' table (columns 2026/2027 and 2027/2028).
tuition.notes: Quote is the table text flattened; the 2027/2028 column reads 'BSc € 20.563' (Dutch number format = EUR 20,563); 2026/2027 is EUR 19,906. Same page: 'You pay the institutional rate if you do not have any of the following nationalities: Dutch or that of another EU/EEA country, Swiss, or Surinamese; or if you do not have a Dutch residence permit that includes entitlement to pay the statutory rate.' A lower transitional rate (EUR 18,175) applies only to students already enrolled in 2025-2026, not to new 2027 entrants. The CSE programme's own tuition subpage (https://www.tudelft.nl/en/onderwijs/opleidingen/bachelors/computer-science-and-engineering/bachelor-of-computer-science-and-engineering/from-application-to-enrollment/tuition-and-fees) still shows the older figure 'Nationality Non-EU/EFTA 2025-2026: € 17.310'.

scholarship_exists.quote: There are no scholarships or financial aid available for students applying to our Bachelor programmes. TU Delft scholarships are only available for students applying to a Master programme.
scholarship_exists.how_found: Web search 'TU Delft scholarship bachelor international students' (site:tudelft.nl) -> Scholarships page (https://www.tudelft.nl/en/education/study-programme-orientation/practical-matters/scholarships) -> 'FAQ' -> section '2. Eligibility and Requirements', question 'Am I eligible for a TU Delft scholarship?'.
scholarship_exists.notes: The central Scholarships page lists only MSc awards (Justus & Louise van Effen Excellence Scholarship; Electrical Engineering/Microelectronics Scholarship), both restricted to applicants admitted to 2-year TU Delft MSc programmes. A TPM student-portal page's share-metadata mentions the Holland Scholarship for non-EEA bachelor's/master's students, but that is a national (Dutch government/Nuffic) programme, not a TU Delft-run award, and the page body only describes MSc scholarships; the FAQ's statement is the authoritative one.

scholarship_international.quote: There are no scholarships or financial aid available for students applying to our Bachelor programmes. TU Delft scholarships are only available for students applying to a Master programme.
scholarship_international.how_found: Same page as scholarship_exists (Scholarships page -> FAQ -> 'Am I eligible for a TU Delft scholarship?').
scholarship_international.notes: No university-run scholarship exists for incoming bachelor applicants, so openness to international applicants cannot be assessed; TU Delft scholarships are for Master applicants only.

access_notes: All pages were fetched successfully from www.tudelft.nl (no login, no blocks). Pages were fetched twice: once via the WebFetch summariser and once via curl so that quotes could be copied verbatim from the HTML.
The programme overview page is largely script-rendered; the static HTML returned only the header facts (title, Language, Numerus fixus, Start, Form, Important dates), which was enough for item 0.
Table quotes (tuition) are the table cells flattened into one line in reading order; the English-test quote joins three consecutive list lines into one sentence.

Kazakhstan is not in TU Delft's published list of secondary diplomas considered equivalent to the Dutch VWO; the site refers such applicants to the Admission Office, so equivalence of the NIS grade-12 diploma is not confirmed on the website.

One local grep command used to extract text from a downloaded page was refused by the sandbox permission classifier; the same text was retrieved with a simpler command. Downloaded copies were kept only in the scratchpad.
